summary: Radar for 4 Oct 2026, the week after EASD. Most of the news is about the next drugs coming after GLP-1s and about keeping muscle. Our best openings are named-drug headline decoders that land in the window before creator coverage catches up. (1) Survodutide's NEJM phase 3 trial (SYNCHRONIZE-2) gives a different weight-loss figure depending on how you count: 13.1% if people stayed on treatment, 9.8% for everyone randomised. Investors called it a disappointment, and that gap is a perfect decoder. (2) Regeneron's trevogrumab with semaglutide cut lean-mass loss to 4.2% vs 7.3%. It's new, it's about muscle, and few creators have covered it. (3) A UK study of 47,039 surgical patients found aspiration or regurgitation under anaesthesia in 1.41% of GLP-1 users vs 0.12% of non-users. It's practical and searchable, and the message is to tell your anaesthetist; it is never advice to stop. Follow-ups on topics already rising: the Lancet's peer-reviewed retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 paper alongside the Connecticut settlement with a 'research-grade' seller, EloraTZP's 23.3% weight loss, orforglipron's heart-safety trial (ACHIEVE-4), the new amylin drugs (petrelintide), and a combined hair-and-nails side-effect explainer. Seasonal and evergreen hooks: foods that support natural GLP-1, postpartum prescribing (needs care), and the 'fat shots' stigma recast as 'what it's approved for'. Microdosing is flagged reject. Older radar topics like 'metabolic whiplash' and the SELECT mediation analysis are fading and left out.

candidates.topic: Survodutide (Boehringer/Zealand) SYNCHRONIZE-2 in NEJM: 13.1% vs 9.8% weight loss at 76 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes and BMI ≥27, depending on how you count
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Did survodutide really get 13%?' Explain the two ways of counting: 13.1% for people who stayed on the 6 mg dose vs about 9.8% for everyone randomised, against 3.1% on placebo. Then explain why investors called it a disappointment next to tirzepatide. Mention that about 18% stopped for stomach side effects vs 1.2% on placebo. It's still a GLP-1/glucagon drug in development and not approved as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Published in NEJM on 1 Oct alongside the EASD presentation. Bloomberg, Fierce, BioSpace and Endpoints all framed it as a letdown. Mainstream health creators haven't decoded the gap between the two counting methods yet. It fits our best title formula: a named drug plus a headline decoder.

evidence.signal: SYNCHRONIZE-2 primary paper, n=752, 3.6 mg and 6 mg vs placebo
Up to 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo at week 76; HbA1c down 0.8–0.9 points
'Underwhelms again in phase 3'; 9.8% figure from the NEJM analysis
Zealand shares fell 12% after the trial flagged side effects

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab + semaglutide: Regeneron's phase 2 COURAGE trial cut lean-mass loss to 4.2% vs 7.3% over 52 weeks
candidates.angle: 'Can a muscle drug stop semaglutide (Wegovy) taking your muscle?' Give the numbers: the 75 mg dose cut lean-mass loss by about 42%, the 25 mg dose was not statistically significant, and an MRI substudy found 69–72% of thigh muscle volume kept. Make clear it's investigational and not yet peer-reviewed. Then pivot to what works today: protein (with the kidney caveat) and strength training.
candidates.why_now: Regeneron's release came out on 1 Oct, with a second wave on 3–4 Oct (Medical Daily, Medical Dialogues). Muscle loss is one of our 'double down' topics, and few YouTube explainers name trevogrumab yet.

evidence.signal: Phase 2 COURAGE confirms lean-mass preservation
Trevogrumab halves semaglutide-induced lean mass loss
Lean mass preserved during and after semaglutide weight loss

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and anaesthesia: aspiration or regurgitation in 1.41% vs 0.12% of patients (UK prospective cohort of 47,039 across 119 sites, Anaesthesia 2026)
candidates.angle: 'On semaglutide or tirzepatide and having surgery or a scope? Tell your anaesthetist.' Explain why slower stomach emptying matters. Give the absolute rates: 1.41% vs 0.12%, mostly while waking up from anaesthesia. Note it's observational. Any plan to pause belongs to the surgical team, never the viewer.
candidates.why_now: The study hit Medical Xpress on 2 Oct, and a PubMed endoscopy review appeared the same week. 'Ozempic before surgery' is a constant search, and this is fresh UK prospective data that consumer creators haven't covered.

evidence.signal: 0.12% vs 1.41% aspiration/regurgitation, OR 11.39, n=47,039
GLP-1 RAs, residual gastric contents and periprocedural management
FDA labelling on pulmonary aspiration with GLP-1 RAs

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide): up to 23.3% weight loss vs tirzepatide alone in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (phase 2, EASD)
candidates.angle: 'Did Lilly's amylin combo beat Mounjaro?' Decode it with the arm, comparator (tirzepatide 15 mg), population (type 2 diabetes), phase 2 size (n=367) and 'not approved'. Tie it to why both Lilly and Novo are now betting on amylin.
candidates.why_now: This is the third snapshot it has appeared in. Coverage has broadened from trade press (Endpoints) to MedPage, Pharmacy Times and Medical Daily, and CNBC ran an explainer on the amylin wave. Search queries like 'what is the new eli lilly drug for weight loss' are spiking.

evidence.signal: 'Best-ever weight loss' in obesity + diabetes
EloraTZP delivers up to 23.3% weight loss
Review of new amylin-based agonists

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 now peer-reviewed in The Lancet (obesity + type 2 diabetes), plus Connecticut's settlement with a 'research-grade' GLP-1 seller
candidates.angle: Attributed correction plus decoder: 'Is retatrutide approved? No, and here's what the Lancet paper actually shows.' Cover the whole-trial average vs the BMI 35+ subgroup (23.4%). Then report that the Connecticut AG says 'research-grade' GLP-1s sold online had impurities and inconsistent doses. Never name or point to any source.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet paper went online on 29 Sep. NDTV, MedPage, the Pharmaceutical Journal and BBC Woman's Hour all covered it, and approval-status searches are spiking. The Connecticut settlement (3 Oct, ABC/GMA) adds a fresh safety hook. Retatrutide corrections already performed for us.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 phase 3 paper
Made-in-China agrees to stop selling 'research grade' GLP-1s to US customers
Settlement details: impurities, contamination, inconsistent dosing

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill ACHIEVE-4 in The Lancet: heart safety matched insulin glargine (MACE HR 0.84) in type 2 diabetes at higher heart risk
candidates.angle: 'Is the orforglipron (Foundayo) pill safe for your heart?' Non-inferiority explained simply: it was shown not worse than insulin, not better. Treat the all-cause death signal (HR 0.43, nominal) with caution. 10.6% stopped the drug. It's a daily pill with no food or water rules.
candidates.why_now: Published in The Lancet on 30 Sep with a Lilly release. Fierce reports Foundayo prescriptions surging while the Wegovy pill stalls, and Stocktwits covered the Foundayo vs oral semaglutide comparison. Pill searches are climbing, and our orforglipron long-form was our top long-form.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4 phase 3 CV safety vs insulin glargine
CV safety plus sustained A1C and weight loss
HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20); all-cause death HR 0.43 nominal; 10.6% discontinued

candidates.topic: Ozempic hair and nails: GLP-1 users reported onycholysis (nail lifting) in 49.2% vs 29.7% of controls (EADV 2026), plus the new study on men predisposed to male-pattern baldness
candidates.angle: Searchable side-effect explainer: 'Is semaglutide (Ozempic) affecting your hair and nails?' Give the numbers and the limits: cross-sectional, self-reported, not peer-reviewed, and only the controls had type 2 diabetes and/or BMI >30. Explain telogen effluvium after rapid weight loss, plus protein and nutrition habits, and when to see a dermatologist.
candidates.why_now: The Washington Post (3 Oct) and ABC30 covered the hair-loss study in men. MedPage, Inc. and the European Medical Journal amplified the nail study. Side-effect topics named after a drug are in our playbook. We posted a nails Short on 10-01, so make this the combined follow-up.

evidence.signal: 575 users vs 1,329 controls; onycholysis 49.2% vs 29.7%
Nail detachment more than 4x as common in first controlled study
Possible connection between GLP-1s and hair loss in men

candidates.topic: Petrelintide (Zealand/Roche) amylin shot: up to 10.7% vs 1.7% weight loss at 42 weeks, with side effects similar to placebo (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology)
candidates.angle: 'Amylin vs GLP-1: is petrelintide the gentler weight-loss shot?' Explain how amylin works (fullness, slower stomach emptying) and give the numbers with the efficacy-estimand label. Then cover why Lilly and Novo are betting on amylin. It's phase 2 and not approved.
keywords: new weight loss shot fewer side effects
candidates.why_now: The Lancet D&E paper came out on 29 Sep and was presented again at EASD. CNBC's 2 Oct piece on the amylin wave is pulling mainstream attention, and creator coverage is still thin.

evidence.signal: ZUPREME-1 phase 2, n=485
10% weight loss, AEs comparable to placebo
Why Lilly and Novo are betting on amylin

candidates.topic: Semaglutide not linked to pancreatic cancer: regulator-mandated Nordic registry study (97,464 matched pairs, HR 0.91, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Safety myth-bust with a named drug: 'Does semaglutide (Ozempic) cause pancreatic cancer?' State the null result exactly (no significant difference), say who was studied, and note it's observational. Pair it with the 'does tirzepatide cause cancer' searches.
candidates.why_now: This is the sixth snapshot with steady momentum. Search-bait queries ('does tirzepatide cause cancer', 'does tirzepatide cause breast cancer') appeared in the last 24 hours, and a new J Surg Oncol breast-cancer paper adds a hook.

candidates.topic: Postpartum GLP-1 prescriptions rose 24-fold: 0.08% to 1.9% of new mothers (JAMA, USC Schaeffer, about 1 million births)
candidates.angle: 'GLP-1 after having a baby: what new moms should ask.' Report who is being prescribed it, starting with type 2 diabetes: about 1 in 6 now start within 6 months. Say plainly that breastfeeding evidence is limited, and give questions to ask your prescriber. No body-shaming, no 'bounce back' language.
candidates.why_now: JAMA published on 1 Oct, followed by US News, Yahoo and News-Medical. A French nationwide Diabetologia pregnancy-safety study came out the same week, and parent communities pick up stories like this fast.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and muscle: a real-world study claims '35% fat loss while preserving muscle', checked against SURMOUNT-1 body-composition data
candidates.angle: Myth-check: 'Does tirzepatide only burn fat?' The news headline comes from a small retrospective study (n=122, 24 weeks). Compare it with trial DXA data showing roughly three-quarters fat and one-quarter lean mass lost. Explain why lean ≠ muscle, then cover protein (kidney caveat) and strength training.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical (2 Oct) amplified it. Paired with trevogrumab and the creatine paper, muscle is the theme of the week, and named-drug mechanism questions are our best format.
